NARRATIVE: on the morning of august 8, 2023, texas eastern began an anomaly dig to expose a geometry feature (buckle/dent) at the 6 o-clock position. the line in this area was very deep (>11-feet). the upstream valve was closed at 09:39 e.t. to lower the line pressure for the excavation and repair. downstream compression was used to help pull the pressure down. while excavating the anomaly, the crew identified indications of a leak at approximately 17:00 et. an operations team was then called in to investigate the suspected leak. at 19:28 et the downstream valve was closed to fully blowdown the line. at approximately 20:30 e.t. it was decided that repairs could likely exceed the phmsa reporting cost threshold. at 21:09 et the national response center was notified. the blowdown was completed on august 9, 2023, at approximately 12:30 et. the line was then excavated and the piping in area of the suspected leak was cut out and removed. an air pressure test was then performed on the cut-out segment and a small through wall feature on the weld (12 o-clock) adjacent to the geometry feature was identified. the pipe was then transported to a lab for further analysis as to the cause. 04/24/2024 supplemental updated part g - apparent cause and part j - integrity inspections the cause of the leak was tensile overloading of the pipe resulting in a 1.5-inch ductile failure at toe of the girth weld. a bending moment exerted high tensile stress near the 12:00 o'clock location and high compressive stress the 6:00 o'clock location, causing the leak at the 12:00 o'clock location and a buckle at the 6:00 o'clock location.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: on august 16, 2023, nng gas control received alarms of low pressure and zero flow at multiple stations in the seminole subsystem, upstream of the kermit, tx, compressor station. the gas controllers contacted customers in the area confirming the pressure and flow deviations. nng operations communications center contacted the field operations team on-call technician to investigate the alarms. nng was notified by local authorities of blowing gas and fire near coyanosa, tx. this confirmed the incident with nng gas control. nng operations communication center initiated an all-call to the kermit, tx, field operations team to respond to the emergency. nng gas control completed shutting-in all receipt and delivery points. the field operations team closed block valve 3 which completed the isolation of the affected segment. first responders closed two roads in the process. the fire from the failure was reduced to burning residual gas within 75 minutes of the segment being isolated. based on lab results, the pipeline ruptured initially in approximately the 6 o'clock position in an area, about a foot long, of severe, mostly circular, pitting and corrosion. this pitting bears all the hallmarks of microbiologically influenced corrosion (mic), a process where one or several strains of bacteria corrode steel. the material had been corroded to approximately 0.041" wall thickness at the rupture origin, approximately 12% of the original material thickness. further examinations of the material did not locate any other failure mechanism.

NAME: KINDER MORGAN TEXAS PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: on july 28, 2023 kinder morgan operations was made aware of audible gas leak. a kinder morgan crude and condensate (kmcc) corrosion technician was working at a shared site with index 145 mlv 759 and heard what appeared to sound like a gas leak. operations were dispatched to valve site. operations measured the leak and determined it was due to a valve stem leak. operations gathered further information and secured the site. plans were made to begin excavation on july 31, 2023 to further investigate. investigation determined a valve packing repair would not be sufficient. the valve would need to be replaced due age and inability to repack the valve stem. the style of valve is an older model walworth gate valve. the original cost estimate to replace the valve was $120,000. the pipeline index 145 serves several major power plants. due to low severity of the leak and ercot guidance, an outage to replace the valve was scheduled for september when demand would not be as high. due to unforeseen installation changes in scope of work to replace the new valve, the cost as of september 15, 2023 were forecasted to exceed $139,700. this incident and repair is now deemed phmsa reportable due to the repair cost exceeding $139,700. total unintentional gas loss of 240 mcf.

NAME: NORTHWEST PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: on november 8, 2023 at 1:09 pm williams operations was notified by an emergency responder of a potential linestrike on the 12" lewiston lateral line located near pullman, wa. operations immediately dispatched technicians to the site as well as the two valves upstream and downstream of the site (valves 34-4 and 34-5). operations technicians were able to close both the upstream and downstream valves at 1:50 pm while other technicians were at the rupture location and confirmed that incident was legitimate and caused by a landowner using a drain tile plow above the pipeline right-of-way. the landowner was not injured, and there were no other injuries associated with the incident. scada systems, located in houston, tx, were also able to confirm the presence of the rupture via rapid pressure drop seen across the line. as a result of the incident, williams lost service at a collection of meter stations downstream of the rupture, namely pullman, moscow, colton, uniontown, genesee, lewiston east, albion, lewiston west, and lewiston pfi meter stations. over the course of the next hour pressure at the rupture location continually relieved through the hole created by the landowner's excavator. operations observed that all pressure had been relieved and noted a 0 psi pressure reading at nearby pullman meter station at 2:27 pm. throughout the next hours operations worked to identify emergency pre-tested stock pipe to send to the site as quickly as possible. operations and construction crews were quickly mobilized on-site that night and began working to get the ruptured line replaced with the new pre-tested stock pipe. the new pipe was installed and x-ray examination was completed on the tie-in welds at 2:53 pm on november 9th, 2023. throughout the next day, operations worked to prepare the affected meter station to begin providing gas to customers again. at 7:15 pm on november 10th, 2023 the entire lewiston lateral was packed to pressure and downstream customers began receiving gas shortly thereafter.

NAME: CONSUMERS ENERGY CO
NARRATIVE: on november 8, 2023, at approximately 12:11 hours consumers energy gas control received an alarm notification which indicated a possible fire at the st. clair compressor station (plant 4 dehydration system building). the consumers energy st. clair compressor station is in ira, michigan (st. clair county). a station mechanic at the site was notified and confirmed activation of the plant fire-gate system occurred due to the fire detection alarm. following the event, the plant was removed from service and the scene was made safe. additional personnel were dispatched to the station to determine the potential cause of the activation. during the incident investigation, no notable indications of failures were present in the facility, but upon arrival, it was noted that a gap in the insulation on the reboiler exhaust stack was clearly visible and was presumed to be the source of a false trip indication to the fire-eye (in direct line of sight) due to the infrared irradiation from the pipe (operating as normal up to 1500 degree f). the insulation on the exhaust system was inspected with no notable issues observed, repaired, and returned to service on november 9, 2023. on november 10, 2023, at approximately 11:17 hours, less than 24 hours after the return to service consumers energy gas control received an alarm notification which indicated a possible fire at the st. clair compressor station (plant 4 dehydration system building). the equipment was taken off-line, and all insulation was removed to permit physical inspection. several cracked welds were identified on the exhaust line of the thermal oxidizer, super heater, and condensate collection system of the thermal oxidizer. loose bolts were found in the flanged connections of the system, and an exhaust pipe slip joint connection to the exhaust stack was found to no longer be inserted into the fitting. both events were reported to mpsc as required when an emergency shutdown system is activated, and gas released. however, a more in-depth visual inspection confirmed additional equipment damage anticipated to exceed phmsa reporting criteria of $139,700. additional investigations after the event have identified a concern relative to insufficient bolt torque specifications used during a 2020 repair to the system, pipe fabrication failure resulting in pre-stress being applied to the failed system connection points, and potential pinned pipe in a high thermal growth area of the system exacerbating stresses imparted to those same connection points. further problem solving is required to determine the root cause of the failure. however, with the concerns defined, consumers energy has taken action to remediate each concern through a refabrication of the super heater vessel failed components, pipe assemblies found to be creating the pre-stress scenario, slip joint insertion was increased to avoid risk of the joint failing, application of torque specifications from the original equipment manufacturer, and implementation of a preventative maintenance schedule for re-validating torque on bolted connections following return to service. further analysis is required to support confirmation of the pipe failure modes identified in the field and is presently underway. the original equipment manufacturer has been engaged in the review and repair plan and is supporting review of the stress analysis. engineering support has been contracted to support model development of the system and execute a pipe stress analysis. following the outcome of the modeling and validation of the failure modes, additional steps may be necessary to improve the integrity of the system and will be implemented accordingly. further analysis confirmed the failure was a result of insufficient bolt torque specifications provided by the manufacturer during a previous repair to the system. the failure was a result of the bolts yielding and torque was lost through the thermal cycle causing bolts to loosen.

9, 2023. on november 10, 2023, at approximately 11:17 hours, less than 24 hours after the return to service consumers energy gas control received an alarm notification which indicated a possible fire at the st. clair compressor station (plant 4 dehydration system building). the equipment was taken off-line, and all insulation was removed to permit physical inspection. several cracked welds were identified on the exhaust line of the thermal oxidizer, super heater, and condensate collection system of the thermal oxidizer. loose bolts were found in the flanged connections of the system, and an exhaust pipe slip joint connection to the exhaust stack was found to no longer be inserted into the fitting. both events were reported to mpsc as required when an emergency shutdown system is activated, and gas released. however, a more in-depth visual inspection confirmed additional equipment damage anticipated to exceed phmsa reporting criteria of $139,700. additional investigations after the event have identified a concern relative to insufficient bolt torque specifications used during a 2020 repair to the system, pipe fabrication failure resulting in pre-stress being applied to the failed system connection points, and potential pinned pipe in a high thermal growth area of the system exacerbating stresses imparted to those same connection points. further problem solving is review of the stress analysis. engineering support has been contracted to support model development of the system and execute a pipe stress analysis. following the outcome of the modeling and validation of the failure modes, additional steps may be necessary to improve the integrity of the system and will be implemented accordingly. further analysis confirmed the failure was a result of insufficient bolt torque specifications provided by the manufacturer during a previous repair to the system. the failure was a result of the bolts yielding and torque was lost through the thermal cycle causing bolts to loosen.

NAME: TRANSCONTINENTAL GAS PIPE LINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on 4/16/2024, operations were performing valve maintenance on pl-115 gate valve (wkm valve with an eim actuator). during the close actuation, the valve failed to stop closing when commanded and resulted in the actuator being push off the stem and into the ground. the end of stroke/limit valve failed to isolate power gas after close, resulting in additional torque energy being applied to the gears housing. all that energy resulted in the failure of the cast iron welds between the actuator and yoke/stem housing. with the gear housing off the shaft, the gate valve could not remain closed and pipeline pressure slammed it open against the bonnet. as a result of the actuator failure, a stainless power gas line broke off and vented. the eim actuator controls were tested on a bench with pressurized air and discovered to successfully achieve the open limit but not the close limit. the cause for this was the close limit valve was installed backwards, which resulted in the poppet being unable to engage with the cam and failure to isolate power gas to the motor once the valve was closed.

NARRATIVE: on wednesday, october 9, 2024, aspen developers corporation (aspen developers) was operating a track hoe to complete road work (grading and drainage) in preparation for a water line installation in the sierra nevada mountains, approximately 3.5 miles east of the washoe county census-designated place of incline village, nevada. while performing work on the existing dirt road, the track hoe operator punctured the top of great basin gas transmission company's (great basin) 8-inch diameter north tahoe lateral gas pipeline with a tooth of the track hoe bucket. the damage occurred at the approximate milepost location of nt-13.56 and resulted in the unintentional release of gas from the steel transmission facility. great basin received notification of the damage at approximately 16:00 pdt on october 9, 2024, by truckee meadows fire and rescue, and promptly dispatched emergency response personnel to the scene for additional investigation and remediation. the pipeline and hazardous material safety administration (phmsa) notification was made to the national response center (nrc) on october 9, 2024, at 20:14 pdt and assigned incident #1413294 due to the natural gas release anticipated to exceed three million cubic feet. great basin did not shutdown the facility to avoid service interruption to a downstream shipper (local distribution company). a repair clamp was used to control the flow of gas on october 10, 2024, at 20:49 pdt. a supplemental notification was made to the nrc on october 14, 2024, at 09:08 pdt and assigned incident #1413672. great basin calculated the total release of gas to total 7,304 mcf . great basin performed a preliminary internal investigation to determine contributing factors associated with the incident on october 16, 2024, and determined that the facility locate marks, established on august 28, 2024, deviated from the actual facility location by 19 feet and the locator incorrectly marked the facility due to bleed off onto a nearby, unmarked steel water line. great basin also determined that the facility locate ticket (2024081500260) used by aspen developers was expired as of september 12, 2024. in addition, and as required by great basin through documentation and verbal communications with the excavator, aspen developers did not notify great basin in advance of excavation to request a high pressure standby, nor did aspen developers pothole great basin facilities to verify location and depth. the repair clamp great basin installed on october 10, 2024 to control the flow of gas was welded onto the impacted area as a permanent repair on october 25, 2024.

NAME: ENBRIDGE GAS OHIO
NARRATIVE: a transmission line leak was identified in ego's gas storage system (group 8) at approximately 16:15 edt on 10/18/2024 near 9232 mudbrook st nw in jackson, oh after a member of the public called in an odor complaint. local personnel utilized valves to shut in the leaking line around 18:00 edt that same day. an original assessment of the costs to replace the line were under the $145,400 operator loss threshold for an incident per 191.3. on 11/5/2024 at approximately 9:20 est, the enbridge gas ohio project manager for the replacement of the section of pipe with the leak informed pipeline safety that costs were now likely to eventually exceed the $145,400 threshold due to higher than expected environmental and contractor costs. the leak was called in as an incident at that time to the ohio public utility commission and the national response center. the section of pipe with the leak has been removed and sent to a 3rd party for analysis. a new section of pipe has been installed to replace the old line but is not yet in service. a supplemental report will be provided with the in-service date and results of the 3rd party lab analysis. 4/25/25 supplemental update: laboratory analysis has been completed. the results of the metallurgical analysis indicate that the leak occurred at an area of discrete pitting from internal corrosion at the bottom of the pipe (6:17 orientation). the leak was likely caused by the presence of an acidic brine (ph 2.92, measured at ambient pressure) with high salinity. the localized corrosion likely occurred at breaks in an otherwise thick protective scale or at areas under deposits at the bottom of the pipe. it is possible that there was a gas phase contribution (i.e., from co2, h2s, and/or 02 corrosion), however, the gas phase contribution was likely secondary to the presence of the acidic brine. the cause of the brine acidity at this location is unknown, but a ph value of 2.92, measured at ambient pressure, is in excess of what is possible from co2 gas dissolved in the process stream. enbridge gas ohio has placed permanent ut gauges on the line for future internal corrosion monitoring. pipeline was placed back into service on 1/7/25. 5/12/2025 updated final report: a14 was changed to "onshore pipeline" to reflect that pipe was considered a transmission asset for regulatory purposes. 5/20/2025: finalizing supplemental report with changes to a14. 1/12/2026: updated final report: c1 was changed from "interstate" to "intrastate".

NAME: HARVEST MIDSTREAM COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on may 19, 2025, harvest initiated a routine foam pigging operation on the pggs system at approximately 11:00 am as part of standard maintenance activities. the pig was launched without incident; however, pressure in the pg-02 segment began to rise unexpectedly later that afternoon. this segment is equipped with a 6-inch pressure relief valve (prv) and emergency shutdown valve (esdv-1), monitored by pressure transmitter pt-201. during the investigation, it was determined that the pig arrived significantly earlier than anticipated. the travel time had been projected using scada flow data. the pig was expected to take up to two days to reach its destination but completed the run within a few hours. this unanticipated arrival led to condensate accumulation in the line, which traveled into the actuator supply tubing of esdv-1, contributing to valve malfunction. at 5:14 pm, pt-201 registered a pressure of 526 psi. the houston control room detected the trend and contacted pipeline operator, who advised that the foam pig was likely still in transit. he informed the controller that the valve had pressure relief capability and instructed them to reset the valve if necessary and notify him if pressure exceeded 600 psi. as pressure continued to rise, pipeline operator initiated manual shut-in coordination with the hilcorp platform. at 5:54 pm, pressure reached 550 psi and esdv-1 received a close command, shutting the valve as designed. however, condensate accumulation in the regulator and actuator tubing subsequently prevented the valve from reopening. the control room issued multiple reset commands to esdv-1 via scada, but the valve remained in an 'error' state and failed to reopen. at 6:37 pm, pressure reached the maop of 606.2 psi, prompting the controller to escalate the situation to operations controls director, foreman, and pipeline operator. by 6:43 pm, scada engineer was contacted for support. he determined that the issue was not due to a scada malfunction but was likely caused by condensate in the regulator and actuator tubing, which prevented the valve from receiving sufficient actuation pressure. at 6:50 pm, pressure peaked at 620.9 psi, exceeding maop but remaining below 110%, and the prv activated to relieve pressure. the prv vented natural gas to atmosphere for approximately 22 minutes. at 6:57 pm, flow through pg-02 dropped to zero. at 7:00 pm, a manual close command was issued to esdv-1, and a permissive signal was received. pipeline operators agreed to keep the valve closed and conduct a stand-up pressure test to confirm pipeline integrity. the test began at 7:18 pm, with pt-201 reading 594.5 psi. by 8:01 pm, pressure had stabilized at 594.0 psi. although the line was deemed safe to restart, repeated attempts to reopen esdv-1 were unsuccessful. at 10:19 pm, pipeline operator and i&e technician decided to keep the system shut-in overnight. the root cause was identified as a liquid-filled regulator and actuator tubing, which prevented proper valve actuation. plans were made to access the site the following morning and replace the affected components.

NARRATIVE: on july 3, 2025, at 16:24 mdt, northern border's gas control (gc) received an alarm at monchy meter station and at 16:36 mdt, gc received a call from a customer about a pressure drop on their compressor station that may have impacted monchy meter station. at 18:38 mdt, a second call was received from the customer asking for a technician on our side to investigate a relief valve at monchy meter station. gc dispatched a technician to investigate a potential release at 18:45 mdt. upon arriving on site at 21:17 mdt, the technician discovered natural gas was being released to the atmosphere through an eight-inch relief valve. immediate action was taken to isolate the valve, which ended the release at 21:20 mdt. the unintentional gas loss was calculated to be approximately 217,850.1 mcf. there were no damages, injuries or hospitalizations. after technicians determined replacement of the pilot valve did not result in reseating, the failed relief valve was removed and sent to a third-party vendor for inspection. the inspection revealed scoring and damage on the main valve piston and piston liner, in addition to deterioration of the main valve seat. the suspected cause of the damage to the valve is accumulation of debris over time, which resulted in the inability of the valve to seal and the unintended release of gas to atmosphere. a secondary relief valve at the monchy meter station is currently providing overpressure protection to the pipeline system.

NARRATIVE: at 8:05 a.m., a fasken operator notified oneok pipeline control center of a gas release at the fasken meter setting. upon receiving the report, pcc called the local measurement technician to head to the site. the tech arrived on site at 9:25 a.m and witnessed a prv releasing gas. the tech isolated the prv at 9:27 a.m. after being isolated, the pressure data was trended, and a pressure change was noted to have occurred at 5:51 a.m. the relief for the valve was removed and sent off for analysis. at this time there are no plans to reinstall a new relief as this is a redundant form of pressure control for this setting. once analysis results have been received a supplemental will be submitted. supplemental- following the event, owt conducted a failure analysis. the analysis concluded that the root cause of the failure was the installation of a prv with a relief tolerance within the normal operating range of the pipeline system. this allowed the pvr to continue to relief within the normal design/operating pressure of the pipeline system. as a result, the pvr stem and seats were damaged, not allowing the pvr to reseat. the pvr is a redundant form of pressure control and has been isolated from the system.

NARRATIVE: on september 10, 2025, at approximately 08:49, a consumers energy employee investigating a potential leak indication confirmed the presence of a leak on line 2600 near the johnson road valve site. line 2600 is a 12-inch natural gas transmission pipeline located in lake city, michigan (missaukee county). consumers energy promptly initiated an isolation procedure to further assess the situation. the affected section of line 2600 was successfully isolated and vented to 0 psig by approximately 16:46 the same day. following excavation, the leak was discovered on a 12-inch ball valve (valve 2622). the valve was preserved in accordance with consumers energy�s failure investigation procedures and transported to the company�s laboratory for analysis. the incident response and remediation efforts were conducted without injury to the public or operating personnel. remediation activities commenced on september 10, 2025. the scope of work included replacement of the 12-inch ball valve and approximately 9-feet of pipeline. the pipeline segment was returned to service on september 23, 2025. further analysis of the failed valve is ongoing to determine the root cause of the failure. laboratory analysis and post-incident investigation determined the leak originated from a failed o-ring within the valve stem assembly inside the bonnet. the failure allowed pressurized natural gas to migrate from the pressure boundary into the valve stem grease bearing cavity which was equipped with a zerk-type greased fitting that included a safety vent feature intended to allow air to escape during greasing operations. once the o-ring failed it allowed and unobstructed path for gas to migrate from the bonnet cavity into the below grade space resulting in a leak to grade.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: on november 2, 2025, at 1712 hours, a senior pipeline technician, for the ogden, iowa, plant team, heard a relief valve venting from his home near the ogden, iowa, compressor station and alerted the on-call technician. the technician arrived to find compressor unit 18 relief valve venting gas. the relief valve was activated due to broken tubing that caused the dome pressure of the relief valve to go to zero psig. additional horsepower was started to ensure throughput was met. at 1755 hours, compressor unit 18 was isolated, shut down and blown down. once the unit was blown down repairs were made to the broken tubing, and the compressor unit was purged and made ready for service. during the investigation it was noted that excessive vibration and insufficient support may have contributed to the tubing failure. support has been added to the device to rectify the vibration concern.

NAME: TEXAS EASTERN TRANSMISSION, LP
NARRATIVE: during the purging operation of a 16-inch offshore pipeline (40-b-03) scheduled for abandonment, a 2-inch temporary hose used for gas venting became disconnected from the 16-inch line approximately two hours into the controlled purge. this disconnection resulted in uncontrolled underwater venting for an estimated five additional hours. the valve and temporary hose assembly were sent to a laboratory for detailed failure analysis. the analysis determined that the 2-inch nipple experienced an axial load combined with bending forces. these forces caused ovalization of the nipple connection and ultimately led to shearing of the threaded connection. the pipeline (40-b-03) had shut down and isolated since october.
